title: OPAG-70: move hook identity out of tracked settings, verify a note lands
summary: OPAG-70 step 4, the last one. .claude/settings.json is tracked and public, and carried OPUM_HOOK_ACTOR/OPUM_HOOK_ACCOUNTABLE_HUMAN (jdnewhouse) in plain sight -- exactly the leak this step exists to close. Moves that env block into .claude/settings.local.json (already gitignored, already carrying a local permissions.allow entry -- merged in, not overwritten), removes the tracked settings.json from git and disk, and gitignores both .claude/settings.json and CLAUDE.local.md going forward so neither can accidentally reintroduce this. Then verifies -- not assumes -- that a hook-written tracker note still lands with the identity read from the now-local file: hooks/flush-state.sh (now living in opum-fleet, still firing here since opum-workflow@opum-fleet is enabled at user scope) swallows the failure silently when the actor/accountable-human env vars are unset, so a broken move looks identical to a working one without this check.

acceptanceCriteria.text: OPUM_HOOK_ACTOR and OPUM_HOOK_ACCOUNTABLE_HUMAN live only in .claude/settings.local.json, merged alongside the existing local permissions block, not replacing it.

.claude/settings.json no longer exists in the repository -- removed from git, not just emptied -- and is added to .gitignore so it cannot silently regain tracked content later. CLAUDE.local.md is added to .gitignore too, pre-emptively (it does not exist yet).

A hook-written tracker note is verified to actually land after the move -- an active In Progress task shows a new note with the opum-marketplace-session actor, not assumed from a clean hook exit alone, since flush-state.sh swallows an actor-unset failure silently.

implementationNotes: AC1/AC2 done: OPUM_HOOK_ACTOR/ACCOUNTABLE_HUMAN live only in .claude/settings.local.json now (merged alongside the existing local permissions.allow entry), .claude/settings.json removed from git and disk, both it and CLAUDE.local.md added to .gitignore. Empirical proof the harness live-injects settings.local.json's env per Bash call, not just at session start: checked `echo $OPUM_HOOK_ACTOR` in this same session immediately after writing the new settings.local.json content -- it read back the new value correctly, despite the session having started before that edit existed. AC3 (verify a note actually lands): fired the real installed hook (opum-fleet's cache copy of flush-state.sh, via CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR pointed at this repo) directly -- exit 0, cursor written correctly, but the note itself was correctly WITHHELD because OMARK-23 and this task were both In Progress simultaneously (the pre-existing ambiguity guard, unrelated to this change, working as designed). Completing this task now leaves OMARK-23 as the sole In Progress task; will fire the hook once more immediately after and check for a landed note there before calling AC3 checked.
finalSummary: Hook identity moved to gitignored settings.local.json, tracked settings.json removed and gitignored against regaining content. AC3 left open pending one more hook fire once this task itself is no longer In Progress (currently ambiguous alongside OMARK-23) -- will check it immediately after, in a follow-up note, once actually observed rather than assumed.
